subject: Crossplane + Helm/Ansible sync for private deployment CI
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
To: CloudOps Team <cloudops@acme-corp.com>, Jared Lim <jared@infra-audit.io>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Crossplane + Helm/Ansible sync for private deployment CI

Hi all,

Putting this thread together to align on how we want to standardize infra modules for private (VPC/on-prem) deployments. Goal: a CI pattern that treats Crossplane as the canonical cloud resource manager (VPCs, subnets, load balancers), Helm for application manifests, and Ansible for host-level configuration where we need imperative steps on bare metal or air-gapped nodes.

What I need from you:
- Review the attached plan (privstack-crossplane-plan.diff) describing the Crossplane composition and resource templates.
- Confirm whether the Helm values file pattern (attached helm-values.example.yaml) is sufficient for templating per-customer overrides and signatures for gated rollouts.
- Validate Ansible artifact packaging and idempotency expectations (see ansible-role-acme.tgz).

Constraints we need to respect:
- Secrets must never land in plaintext in CI logs; KMS/HSM integration required for secrets retrieval steps.
- Terraform state / Crossplane claims will be stored in the customer VPC (s3-compatible object store) and mirrored to our audited vault for snapshotting. Need to ensure we have a repeatable reconciliation process.
- CI must block on an automated security check (static analysis + policy engine) before any Crossplane composition is applied to an on-prem environment.

Proposed cadence: two-week gating branch where infra changes land in a feature branch, go through automated acceptance tests (unit + smoke), then a canary apply to a staging private customer environment, then full apply.

I'll collate feedback and produce a short PR checklist for module authors. Please reply with redlines by EOD Thursday.

Thanks,
Sofia
Sofia Ivanova
Head of Platform Partnerships
Redwood Inference
From: Jared Lim <jared@infra-audit.io>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: CloudOps Team <cloudops@acme-corp.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-28T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Crossplane + Helm/Ansible sync for private deployment CI

Sofia,

Thanks for the concise brief — good separation of concerns. A few early thoughts after a quick pass of the attachments:

1) Crossplane/composition drift: ensure you include a reconciliation window and a recorded operator action log. We recommend a dedicated status bucket for operator actions (append-only) that we can ingest into your audit pipeline.

2) State storage: storing tfstate or Crossplane claims in the customer VPC is fine, but you need a signed snapshot process (at least daily) back to your audit store with encryption-in-transit and attestations in the snapshot metadata.

3) CI gating: add an explicit policy step that verifies Helm charts against a curated policy (e.g., image registries allowed, no hostNetwork unless tagged). Tools: we've used conftest + Open Policy Agent for this layer.

4) Ansible artifacts: tarballs are OK, but include checksums in a manifest and have the CI verify signatures before execution. Also, document expected idempotency for each role.

I can run a quick policy audit next week if you want; it's helpful to have a short checklist per module.

— Jared
Jared Lim
Infra Audit (contractor)
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>

On Wed, Apr 28, 2027 at 11:03 AM Jared Lim <jared@infra-audit.io> wrote:
> Sofia,
>
> Thanks for the concise brief — good separation of concerns. A few early thoughts after a quick pass of the attachments:

All good suggestions — quick technical notes from the infra side:

- KMS integration: for on-prem we should rely on a customer-managed HSM or KMS endpoint; CI runners will request short-lived credentials via our vault proxy. We should add a vault-step plugin to the Crossplane apply job that exchanges a CI token for read-only secrets scoped to the specific composition.

- Crossplane providers: prefer to pin provider versions (provider-aws, provider-gcp, provider-helm) in the composition CRs to avoid surprise upgrades. We'll add a provider-lock file to the repo.

- Helm: helm-values.example.yaml looks fine, but we should add a forbidden list for mutable cluster-wide primitives (ClusterRoles, NodeSelectors with hostNetwork). Enforcement via CI policy makes sense.

- Ansible: switch to signed collections (ansible-galaxy collection format) rather than raw tar gz. That helps with provenance and signatures. If we keep tarballs, add .sig files and require verification in the runner.

Action items I can take:
- Draft a provider-lock + versioning guide for Crossplane compositions.
- Add a vault proxy example for short-lived secrets in the CI job.

Rishi
Principal Infra Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-04-29T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Crossplane + Helm/Ansible sync for private deployment CI

Thanks — quick product/ops perspective:

- Rollout strategy: agree on the canary stage, but add a manual gating step for the first two customers in a region (product constraints require approval for customer-impacting infra). We should enumerate the exact signal thresholds that cause automatic rollback (failed readiness probes for N minutes, database migration errors, etc.).

- Version pinning: put version gates on the CI pipeline so that major provider upgrades require an explicit approval in the deployment ticket (link to ticket template in the PR checklist).

- Observability: ensure each apply run emits standardized metrics (apply_duration, reconcile_errors, drift_detected) and traces we can correlate to customer incidents. Expose those in the Redwood Console per-route dashboards.

- PR checklist: add items for acceptance test artifacts (screenshots/log snippets), signed artifact checksums, provider-lock file, and an owner tag for rollback contact.

Will review the PR checklist draft once it's up.

— Lauren
Director, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

Thanks everyone — great feedback. Summarizing action items and owners:

1) Rishi: provider-lock + versioning guide and example provider-lock file (PR target: repo infra/crossplane/ by 2027-05-06).
2) Rishi + Markus: vault-proxy example and CI job snippet that does the short-lived secrets exchange (attach to CI pipelines doc).
3) Lauren: finalize rollout signals and approval checklist (will add thresholds and the manual gating requirement for first customers).
4) Markus: convert Ansible packaging recommendation to signed collections or add detached .sig verification step (aim to prototype by 2027-05-05).
5) Jared: optional policy audit once the PR checklist is available (thanks — can scope to the three highest-risk rules).

I'll open a tracking epic (INFRA-4521) and a PR checklist doc in the Drive. Please comment on the PR checklist when I post it; I'll include the links in the epic and the PR template.

Attachments referenced: privstack-crossplane-plan.diff, helm-values.example.yaml, ansible-role-acme.tgz (checksums and sigs to follow).
